blocks.content: Every HTTP topic covered so far in this course has been built around paths, methods, and status codes, the standard REST style pattern. gRPC takes a genuinely different approach: instead of thinking in terms of paths and HTTP methods, a client calls a method directly, almost exactly like calling an ordinary function in regular application code.

This topic introduces gRPC at a foundational level, what makes it genuinely different, and specifically why many real, high volume backend systems choose it for internal service to service communication.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784017890875-152433259.png
blocks.alt: gRPC lets a client call a remote method directly, feeling almost exactly like an ordinary local function call

blocks.content: 1. A Genuinely Different Mental Model

A typical REST API, exactly the pattern covered throughout the http-methods topic, is built around paths and HTTP methods, GET /items, POST /items, and so on. gRPC instead defines actual named methods directly, and calling one over the network feels remarkably close to calling an ordinary function in regular application code, not constructing a URL and picking an HTTP verb at all.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784017892932-797723415.png
blocks.alt: A typical REST API is built around paths and methods; gRPC lets a client call remote methods almost like local functions

blocks.content: 2. Protocol Buffers: A Compact, Efficient Format
blocks.text: 2. Protocol Buffers: A Compact, Efficient Format

blocks.content: Where a typical REST API commonly exchanges data as JSON, readable text but genuinely larger and slower to parse, gRPC instead uses Protocol Buffers, a compact, efficient binary format specifically designed to encode and decode data quickly, with meaningfully smaller messages traveling over the network for the exact same actual data.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784017894718-878735786.png
blocks.alt: Protocol Buffers use a compact binary format, producing smaller messages that are faster to encode and decode than JSON

blocks.content: 3. Built Directly on HTTP 2

gRPC is built directly on top of HTTP 2, specifically inheriting its multiplexing capability covered in the http-versions topic, letting many separate gRPC calls efficiently share one single underlying connection at once, without one call blocking the others.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784017896520-568740814.png
blocks.alt: gRPC is built directly on HTTP 2, inheriting its multiplexing to let many calls efficiently share one connection

blocks.title: A direct, concrete payoff from an earlier topic
blocks.content: This is a genuinely concrete, real world example of why HTTP 2 multiplexing, covered as a somewhat abstract improvement in the http-versions topic, actually matters in a real, production system built on top of it.
4. A Strict, Contract First Design

Before any actual code is written, gRPC requires a strict schema defining every single method and the exact shape of every message up front. Client and server code is then automatically generated directly from that shared schema, guaranteeing both sides always agree on the exact contract, with far less room for the kind of subtle mismatches that can creep into a loosely defined REST API over time.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784017898041-47164141.png
blocks.alt: A strict schema defines every method and message shape up front, with client and server code generated automatically from it

5. Genuine Streaming Support

Beyond a simple request and response, gRPC genuinely supports several real streaming modes. A server can stream many separate responses back over time for one single request. A client can stream many requests over time. Both sides can even stream simultaneously at once, genuinely useful patterns a typical REST request and response exchange does not naturally support at all.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784017899885-750427886.png
blocks.alt: gRPC genuinely supports streaming in either direction, or both simultaneously, beyond a simple single request and response

6. Why This Combination Genuinely Performs Well
blocks.text: 6. Why This Combination Genuinely Performs Well

blocks.content: The compact binary encoding means meaningfully less data actually travels over the network. The HTTP 2 foundation means connections are reused efficiently across many calls. Together, this combination genuinely produces lower latency, a real, practical advantage specifically for high volume, internal service to service calls where performance at scale actually matters.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784017901572-951784760.png
blocks.alt: Compact binary encoding plus an efficient HTTP 2 foundation together produce genuinely lower latency at scale

blocks.title: This matters most at real, meaningful scale
blocks.content: For a handful of occasional calls, the performance difference is genuinely negligible. It is specifically at high call volume, many internal services talking constantly, that this combination of advantages actually shows up as a meaningful, measurable difference.
7. When gRPC Is Actually the Right Choice
blocks.text: 7. When gRPC Is Actually the Right Choice

blocks.content: For internal service to service calls, especially at high volume with genuine low latency needs, gRPC is a genuinely strong, well suited fit. For public facing APIs that need to be broadly, easily accessible, readable in a browser, callable with simple, ubiquitous tools, a REST API is often the more practical choice, forward pointer to the dedicated rest-vs-grpc topic next in this module for the full comparison.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784017903166-678417756.png
blocks.alt: Internal, high volume service calls favor gRPC; broadly accessible public APIs often favor the simpler, more universal REST

Assuming gRPC is always the objectively better choice, when a typical REST API broad accessibility and simplicity is often the more practical fit for public facing needs.

It uses Protocol Buffers, a compact binary format, rather than typical JSON text.
It is built directly on HTTP 2, inheriting genuine multiplexing benefits.
